papers.title: Investigation on Porosity and Microhardness of 316L Stainless Steel Fabricated by Selective Laser Melting
papers.abstract: This study investigates the porosity and microhardness of 316L stainless steel samples fabricated by selective laser melting (SLM). The porosity content was measured using the Archimedes method and the advanced X-ray computed tomography (XCT) scan. High densification level (≥99%) with a low average porosity content (~0.82%) were obtained from the Archimedes method. The highest porosity content in the XCT-scanned sample was ~0.61. However, the pores in the SLM samples for both cases (optical microscopy and XCT) were not uniformly distributed. The higher average microhardness values in the SLM samples compared to the wrought manufactured counterpart are attributed to the fine microstructures from the localised melting and rapid solidification rate of the SLM process.

summary_en.motivation: To characterize porosity and microhardness of 316L stainless steel fabricated by selective laser melting.
summary_en.method: Porosity was measured using Archimedes method and X-ray computed tomography, while microhardness was tested via Vickers indentation.
summary_en.result: SLM samples achieved high densification (≥99%) and higher microhardness than wrought counterparts due to fine microstructure.
summary_en.validation: Experimental validation through multiple porosity measurement techniques and microhardness testing.

papers.title: Prevention of Periprosthetic Joint Infections of the Hip and Knee.
papers.abstract: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) is a rare but devastating complication of arthroplasty. Research has been dedicated to minimizing the incidence of PJI, leading to the development of a comprehensive perioperative approach. Multiple preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative factors can increase patient risk. From medical management and skin sterilization to wound sterility and blood management, multiple issues must be considered in a well-rounded prevention protocol. In this literature review, we consolidate the current information that orthopedic surgeons can use to minimize PJI after total knee arthroplasty and total hip arthroplasty.
